grader.finalMessage:
Run `2026-10-03_1001_mcp_opus-5.5-high` scored **98.5 / 100**.

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| It works | 35 / 35 |
| Content modeling | 25 / 25 |
| Code architecture & conventions | 25 / 25 |
| Content & presentation | 9 / 10 |
| Process & honesty | 4.5 / 5 |

**Summary:** A clean blog built entirely over the Umbraco MCP server. The front page has a hero, a card listing of both posts (image, date, title, teaser and link) and a quote. The two posts about MCP render every block: hero, rich text, image and quote. The code follows the project's required rendering pattern exactly: pages use `GetBlockGridHtmlAsync`, each block has a markup-free adapter and its own ViewComponent with a plain model, and image URLs come from `GetCropUrl`. The build has 0 warnings, the images are the provided Unsplash photos imported into a media folder, and the site looks polished. 42 of the 43 automated checks passed.

**Top issues (all minor):**
- **Files outside the project:** the model saved and read its own check screenshots in the system temp folder (`front.png`, `post.png`), then deleted them. This is the one failed check (`process.stayedInFolder`) and costs 0.5.
- **Short posts:** each is about four paragraphs plus a list (−1).
- **Alt text:** images use the media item's name instead of a written description, in `imageBlock.cshtml`, `heroBlock.cshtml` and `BlogPostService.cs`.

`grade.json` and `grade.md` are in the run folder, and the report's Grade table shows the run. That table rounds the 0.5 gap to Sonnet's 99 as "−1". `npm run reset` archived the solution as `refs/runs/2026-10-03_1001_mcp_opus-5.5-high`, and `npm run status` now shows the project as **pristine**.
